## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Oktober 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.173
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.173
- Datum: 10.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
c/o EDITORA GUANABARA
132, RUA OUVIDOR
RIO DE JANEIRO

PETROPOLIS, (BRASIL)
(34, RUA GONÇALVES DIAS)

Dear Hannah and Manfred, we came down for one day to Rio to bid farewell
to our friends Wiener Morgenthau who leave in two days for Newyork. It is for us
already a strange feeling to be again in a big town because we live in Petropolis and
a peasant life. All is primitive - Lotte will here give you details about the
cooking - but this has a great charm; isolation in these moments is a kind of
happiness and I have there my natural life, resting, working and I feel myself
much more useful than in Newyork. We really wanted some rest after these
long months and I am unfortunately convinced that our nerves in the next
months and years have to be prepared for strenuous times; I am glad that
Lotte likes this retired life as much as I do. For the moment I cannot
imagine that I ever would like to live otherwise than in this retired way
but who can tell was it expecting still us all? In this country you feel
that one can live with very few money and that one does not really
want much from life, while in Newyork you are much more occu-
pied with material things. A foreigner who does not know us would call
our life here monotonous and tedious, but you know how we like quiet
walks, quiet resting - altogether we went one single time to the Cine-
ma, we have no wish to see and to hear much except from you. I have
really resigned to see anything sooner before and I feel much better
~~not~~ not more to be troubled by hopes and fears; in my age one has
to learn the „vita contemplativa“ and to leave all fame and wealth
to the others. We are not quite sure if we shall not have a day -
only we fear to get attached if one day we has to move or to leave
again. - I hope that you have followed my advice and do not worry
about the house in Bath, I see no reason why you should love
your time with lost things and I am sure that Mrs Baumann
will it keep in good order. My dear, I know how full your life is and
how many things Manfred & you have to do and it is for me a
disagreeable feeling that you should care for our things, which are
as all others subject to all dances and will be after more a
barden than a pleasure. Please go only there if you like it for
yourself and not out of a sentiment of duty against us. We are et-

[Randnotiz links:]
peching your news about Manfred and if he will find the right position. From our
little life in this area there is no more to report - so only
heartfelt regards to all and love to you both
Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Briefpapier mit gedrucktem Briefkopf. Die Tinte ist violett. Die Randnotiz am linken Rand ist vertikal geschrieben.
